title: SC PSC Order No. 2026-154H(A) — Amended Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Accepting Power Purchase Agreement and Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Power Purchase Agreement Between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC and Chester PV1, LLC
summary: Amended Standing Hearing Officer Directive Order Accepting Power Purchase Agreement and Granting Request for Confidential Treatment - Power Purchase Agreement Between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC and Chester PV1, LLC
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF SOUTH CAROLINA 

AMENDED STANDING HEARING OFFICER DIRECTIVE 

DOCKET NO. 2026-163-E ORDER NO. 2026-154-H(A) 

JULY 8, 2026 

STANDING HEARING OFFICER: C. Jo Anne Wessinger Hill, Esquire 

DOCKET DESCRIPTION: DOCKET NO. 2026-163-E – Power Purchase Agreement Between 
Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC and Chester PV1, LLC 

MATTER UNDER CONSIDERATION: Request by Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC (DEC) for 
the Commission to grant Confidential Treatment to the Power Purchase Agreement (“PPA” or 
“Agreement”) between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC (DEC) and Chester PV1, LLC (Chester PV1) 
filed on June 25, 2026 (DEC Letter/Request). 

HEARING OFFICER’S ACTION: The amendment to the July 7, 2026 Standing Officer 
Directive when compared with this July 8, 2026 Amended Standing Hearing Officer Directive is 
a correction of an inadvertent typographical error replacing the name of the Duke Company from 
“Progress” in certain places with the name of “Carolinas” to reflect Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, 
as described in the docket above. There is no change related to the Request for Confidential 
Treatment as granted. 

This matter comes before the Hearing Officer on a Request by DEC pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. 
section 58-41-20(E)(1), S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804 and Commission Order No. 2005-226, as 
amended by Orders No. 2020-490 and 2023-859, seeking Confidential Treatment of certain 
portions of the Power Purchase Agreement between DEC and Chester PV1. Section 58-41-
20(E)(1) mandates that all electric “utilities shall file with the commission power purchase 
agreements entered into pursuant to PURPA, resulting from voluntary negotiation of contracts 
between an electrical utility and a small power producer not eligible for the standard offer.” S.C. 
Code Ann. § 58-41-20(E)(1) (Supp. 2025) (emphasis added). 

In submitting the filing, DEC asserts that “[d]ue to the commercial sensitivity and proprietary 
nature of certain portions of the Agreement, DEC respectfully requests that the Commission find 
that, pursuant to S.C. Code Ann. Regs. 103-804(S)(2) and S.C. Code Ann. § 30-4-40(a)(1), certain 
provisions of the Agreement are exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, 
S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq.” DEC Letter/Request, p. 1. DEC further asserts that 
confidentiality is sought for the identified confidential information and relevant provisions of the 
Agreement for which DEC “derives economic value” from such information “not being generally 
known to, and not being readily ascertainable by proper means, by other persons who would be 
able to obtain economic value from its disclosure.” Id. Additionally, DEC states that the redacted 
and confidential provisions are “confidential pricing and conditions, as well as delivery parameters 
and details of the operating characteristics of the facility, all of which are proprietary and specific 
to this counter-party [Chester PV1].” Id. DEC further states that the specific redactions and 
confidentiality in the Agreement were mutually reviewed and agreed upon by both DEC and 
Chester PV1, as well as the parties agreeing not to disclose any term of these confidential 
provisions to a third party without the prior written consent of the other party. Id.

DOCKET NOS. 2026-163-E 
JULY 8, 2026

Commission Regulation 103-804(S)(2) provides that the Commission, within its discretion, can 
determine what matters are placed and available in the public record on the DMS. S.C. Code Ann. 
Regs. 103-804(S)(2) (2012). Likewise, the Commission has discretion to determine what matters 
are exempt from public disclosure, including exemption from release under the Freedom of 
Information Act, S.C. Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. Id. 

In support of the Request and in protection of this information, DEC complied with the 
requirements of Commission Order 2005-226, as amended by Orders No. 2020-490 and 2023-859. 
Additionally, DEC provided a confidential version and a redacted public version of the Agreement 
to the Commission and the Office of Regulatory Staff. There were no objections to the Request 
for Confidential Treatment requested by DEC. 

Considering the Request of DEC and acts in compliance with Orders No. 2005-226, 2020-490, 
and 2023-859, the Hearing Officer finds that confidential treatment of the Power Purchase 
Agreement between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, and Chester PV1, LLC, is warranted. 
Accordingly, the Request for Confidential Treatment filed by Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, 
is granted as requested. The Power Purchase Agreement between Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, 
and Chester PV1, LLC, is exempt from disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act, S.C. 
Code Ann. §§ 30-4-10 et seq. The Commission shall maintain the confidential version of this 
Agreement as confidential unless or until the Commission rules such information is not entitled to 
protection from public disclosure, or Duke Energy Carolinas, LLC, and Chester PV1, LLC, agree 
that such information is no longer confidential, commercially sensitive, or proprietary. 

The Hearing Officer further accepts for filing the Power Purchase Agreement between Duke 
Energy Carolinas, LLC, and Chester PV1, LLC, on behalf of the Commission. 

This concludes the Hearing Officer’s Directive.
